At Most One of Many Is One Row, Not One Row per Pair

recorded.prompt:q-precheck: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-precheck: If a group has fewer candidates than $`k`$, no plan reaches $`k`$. Candidates that exclude each other count once: two projects in the same alternative group can never both be funded.

recorded.prompt:q-precheck:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-precheck:a: "Plains has two transmission candidates, P001 and P002, so 'at least 2' looks possible; but they are the replace and repair options for the same asset ... and a plan may fund only one of them." Raw candidate counts mislead.
recorded.prompt:q-precheck:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-precheck:c: Applying `most_choosable` ("each alternative group counts once"): P3 is outside the group and counts on its own, so 1 + 1 = 2, not 1.
recorded.prompt:q-precheck:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-precheck:d: The precheck is "fewer than $`k`$ choosable in $`S`$ (each alternative group counts once)". An at-least row with k no larger than the choosable count passes, so not every such row is infeasible.
recorded.prompt:q-clique:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-clique:a: "Both allow exactly the same 0/1 plans ... So both MILPs have the same optimum."
recorded.prompt:q-clique:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-clique:b: "Both allow exactly the same 0/1 plans ... So both MILPs have the same optimum."
recorded.prompt:q-clique:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-clique:c: "one row ... LP bound $24,197.20k ... pairs 15 rows LP bound $24,515.10k". The count row (B) gives the tighter bound, not the looser one.
recorded.prompt:q-switch:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-switch:b: The page needs the second row to say, for g = 0, that the count "is at most 0. No vegetation work". With n <= 5, g = 0 allows n = 1 or 2.
recorded.prompt:q-switch:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-switch:c: n >= 3 is always on, so it never allows "no vegetation work at all". The page switches it with "the first row says the count is at least 0" when g = 0.
recorded.prompt:q-switch:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-switch:d: Applying the page's case reading: at g = 0 the rows give n >= 3 and n <= 0, which no plan meets. At g = 1 they give n >= 0, which allows 1 or 2. The page's first row is $`\ge k\, g_r`$.
